surface: USB / companion attack surface and TrustZone NS isolation (key=usb). Threat model: malicious host drives NS world; NS pointer games across NSC; USB stack bugs; protocol parsing; companion substitutes data; DoS/wedge. Inventory built by reading nonsecure/src/usb/*, nonsecure/src/{main,nsc_api}.rs, shared/src/{apdu_framing,ns_ptr_validate}.rs, secure/src/nsc/{mod,ptr_validate,ns_ptr,state,cmd_*}.rs, secure/src/{sau,timeout}.rs, secure/src/hw/{iwdg,tzic,usb_hw}.rs, secure/src/main.rs exception handlers, fuzz/, CI/Makefile, docs/companion/usb-protocol-v2.md, docs/security/{threat-model,production-security,HARDENING,usb-fw-update-hardening}.md, the two adversarial-review playbooks (usb-companion, trustzone-gateway), and ~40 open GitHub issues. Baseline posture: NS world is untrusted by design (holds no secret); the only load-bearing boundary is the NSC gateway + SAU/GTZC; NS-side bugs are DoS-class.

has.item: HID frame reassembly state machine lives in the dependency-free shared crate (production == fuzz harness): 3/5/7-byte prefix checks, MAX_APDU_RX=4096 cap, zero-length/oversize reject, channel-ID isolation (foreign seq=0 and foreign continuation frames are dropped without scrubbing the owner), same-channel desync aborts + scrubs partial bytes, checked_add bounds before every copy
has.notes: PingEcho (tag 0x02) echoes the attacker frame verbatim back to host (transport.rs:461-464) — harmless.

has.item: APDU header parser with Lc overrun check (checked_add) and CLA/INS routing; GET_RESPONSE (0xC0) is deliberately CLA-agnostic

Chained-APDU state machine: INS-swap mid-chain resets, overflow-safe cursor vs caller capacity, per-CMD accumulation bound (per_cmd_chain_bound) so a bogus INS cannot burn the ~8 KB global CHAIN_BUF; chained-INS allowlist is checked BEFORE chain.step accepts any bytes
has.notes: usb-fw-update-hardening.md §5 finding #4 still lists the per-CMD bound as open LOW while §9 says it is already had — doc is internally inconsistent; code has it.

has.item: Chained-command TOTAL lifetime bound (30 s, not idle-reset) with router-lease release on expiry (X17-UC1 / F2)
has.notes: Issue #136 (X17-UC1) is still OPEN although the fix landed in 22c5d614 ('absolute chain-lifetime + drain caps on the router lease (#147)'). Clock is host-driven FNSOF (see gap #428).

has.item: GET_RESPONSE drain protections: 30 s inter-chunk idle timeout, 120 s absolute drain deadline not reset by keepalives, scrub of pending cursor on any non-GET_RESPONSE command, FI-clamped chunk length
Transport RX reassembly timeout (5 s on the OTG_DSTS.FNSOF frame clock) scrubs a half-assembled APDU; deadline only cleared when the owner's stream actually died (GPT-5.6 wave finding)

Single-session router lease (F11): a foreign HID channel is refused with SW 0x6985 while another channel owns a live chain or drain, without disturbing the owner's state; lease re-derived after every dispatch

FI-hardened length clamp `fi_min` (black_box barrier + opposite-branch recompute) at every host-influenced copy: HID first/continuation frame, TX queue, GET_RESPONSE chunk; IR regression gate `make check-fi-ir` exists
has.notes: check-fi-ir is NOT invoked from .github/workflows/*.yml (grep empty) — the gate exists but is not CI-executed. Issue #130 still OPEN although the black_box fix is in the tree.

has.item: OTG hardening in NS: FDMOD=1 (device-only, no role switch), SOF interrupt masked (timing side-channel), VBUS sensing overridden for USB-C
has.notes: usb-companion playbook Part B item 3 cites secure/src/hw/usb_hw.rs for FDMOD/SOF; it actually lives in the NS crate (playbook UC5 row already corrects this).

has.item: USB OTG FS deliberately left NS in GTZC (SECCFGR3 bit 10) and the NS USB stack owns DWC2; OTG_FS has no DMA so every USB byte is CPU-mediated and subject to SAU/GTZC; only the USB pads are handed to NS (pq1: PA11/PA12 only — PA15/PB5/PB15 stay secure; board const asserts)
has.notes: pq1 enumeration confirmed with GPIOA_SECCFGR=0xe7ff (usb_hw.rs:18-19).

has.item: GTZC1 TZSC default-secure allowlist (I2C1/I2C2 [+I2C4 on pq1], IWDG when selected, UCPD1, TIM2/TIM3, SPI1 under ui-lcd, AES/HASH/RNG/PKA/SAES) with exact-equality compile-time image pins for all four IWDG×board combos and fail-closed post-write `verify_or_halt` readback
has.notes: GTZC2 (TAMP/BKPSRAM) is NOT configured or locked — the one acknowledged follow-up.

has.item: MPCBB block-based SRAM attribution: SRAM1 (192 KB) all secure, SRAM2 (64 KB) all NS; SAU regions 0-3 (NS flash, NSC veneers from linker symbols, NS SRAM, NS peripherals); proto NS pointer windows compile-time asserted to be subsets of the SAU NS regions in both the secure crate and the Kani-harness crate

tz-2 security-config freeze after programming: SYSCFG CSLCKR LOCKSAU|LOCKSVTAIRCR, GTZC1 TZSC_CR.LCK, AIRCR PRIS=1 (secure IRQs outprioritize NS), BFHFNMINS=0 (faults taken secure), SYSRESETREQS under mode-production; AIRCR low-half-word config bits AND lock bits read back via verify_or_halt
has.notes: Silicon receipt of boot+gtzc-enforcement AFTER the lock is still owed (playbook TZ9 residual). trustzone-gateway playbook TZ10 still says the AIRCR verify is missing — stale.

has.item: TZIC illegal-access IRQ (NVIC 8) armed with the same masks as TZSC; counts violations, snapshots SR; under `tzic-wipe` (forced ON for shipping dual-SE images by the nsc/mod.rs MEDIUM-1 fence) a single NS→S illegal access triggers zeroize + page-125 wipe-arm + USB soft-disconnect + reset
has.notes: TZIC IER4=0: AHB3/memory-group probes (FLASH, GPDMA1, TZSC/TZIC, MPCBB) are hardware-blocked but uncounted — accepted instrumentation gap (sau.rs:610-629).

has.item: NS pointer range validation: pure window arithmetic (null, usize→u32 truncation, u32 wrap, NS-SRAM-or-flash containment, mailbox disjointness) is host-shared, Kani-proven unbounded with non-vacuity controls, Miri-tree-borrows-checked; firmware ANDs in the ARMv8-M TT/SAU re-classification per 32-byte stride
has.notes: TT is a deliberate `true` stub off-target (ptr_validate.rs:123-140); TT semantics are only exercised on silicon.

has.item: `NsPtr<T>` → `ReadPtr`/`WritePtr` typestate with F-8 double-sentinel validation
has.notes: Adopted by exactly one veneer (nsc_register_heartbeat); all production cmd_* handlers use the legacy free functions (grep: only ns_ptr.rs and mod.rs reference NsPtr). threat-model.md:263 and red-teaming.md §8.1 describe the typestate as THE mechanism.

has.item: Every production handler that takes NS pointers gates them through `fi::check_true_into_sentinel(|| validate_ns_*_ptr)` (FI FAIL-IN shape), and the three sign handlers re-validate the output write extent at the deref site (finding F5) so a single branch-skip cannot reach an OOB write
has.notes: Exceptions: cmd_pin_attempt_log.rs:23 uses a bare `if !validate_ns_write_ptr` (no sentinel, no HandlerGuard, reachable without PIN); prodtest.rs has 15 bare gates (#140 says 12).

has.item: TOCTOU snapshot discipline: per-byte `read_volatile` copy of the NS payload into the secure-SRAM `SIGN_SNAP_BUF` (shared by the three sign handlers, wiped before fill, const-asserted ≤ buffer), parse only the copy; manifest likewise snapshotted onto the S-stack

Companion-supplied fields treated as assertions, not authority: entry_point compared twice to ENTRY_POINT_V06 through independent sentinel gates before any parse; wire `sender` must equal the independently derived CREATE2 address for account_index (sender binding, CFI-stepped); slot key derived from (entropy, chain_id, slot_index) so a slot/chain lie yields a different key, never reuse

PIN gate on every secret-touching gateway command via FihBool complement-storage read through a Hamming-distant sentinel; `HandlerGuard`/HANDLER_DEPTH (AtomicU32) enforces non-reentrancy and blocks the SysTick idle-wipe while a handler holds stack copies of secrets
has.notes: Handlers without a guard: cmd_lock, cmd_is_unlocked, cmd_get_remaining, cmd_pin_attempt_log (short, no secret copies).

has.item: NS boot handover clears all GP registers, sets MSP_NS/PSP_NS/CONTROL_NS=0 and BXNS; CMSE `cmse-nonsecure-entry` veneers are thin wrappers that build GatewayArgs and delegate to the same cmd_*::run used by the QEMU mailbox path (QEMU args are snapshotted before dispatch)
has.notes: FPU register clear omitted because FPU not enabled (boot_ns.rs:54-57) — must be revisited if FPU is ever turned on.

has.item: S-only inactivity timer (120 s): NS gateway pings do not reset it; `confirm` does not reset on entry (HIGH-13); REQUEST_UNLOCK arms the window only when the device is LOCKED with no secret loaded (#713)
REQUEST_UNLOCK is idempotent when already unlocked (F3) so a hostile host cannot re-pop PIN prompts on an unlocked device
has.notes: When the device is LOCKED each INS 0x10 still pops the trusted PIN dialog; nothing bounds how often a host may do that (see gaps).

has.item: Secure-owned IWDG (Secure alias 0x5000_3000, SECCFGR1 bit 7) fed from SysTick only while a verified tick pair + CFI word are present; progress = NS heartbeat advanced OR busy handler (capped at 30 s, rr-2) OR trusted-UI wait AND !idle; 4 s stall limit; forced ON for stm32u585+mode-production; heartbeat address validated through the FI-doubled NsPtr typestate
has.notes: Silicon denial receipts for NS CPU/GPDMA reload attempts are still owed (#79). IWDG detects a STALLED loop, not a FLOODED one (threat-model.md:374).

has.item: Fault/abnormal-path secret hygiene: HardFault (incl. NS faults, since BFHFNMINS=0) and unexpected IRQs zeroize SRAM secret caches then sys_reset (not the destructive SE wipe); panic handler zeroizes, paints a fatal screen, and parks in WFI; NS USB builds use panic_halt so an NS panic becomes an IWDG reset
has.notes: HARDENING.md:376 says the panic handler 'wipes secrets and resets' — it halts (WFI), it does not reset.

has.item: OFFCHAIN_SYNC (companion-chosen durable floor) hardened against page-123 exhaustion and value-inflation bricks: clamp to OFFCHAIN_COUNT_CEILING, trusted-display consent for new slot or floor raise, MAX_DISTINCT_SLOTS=128 structural cap at the flash write chokepoint, display↔commit binding re-checked through a sentinel
GET_WALLET_ADDRESS optional `show` flag (#472) paints the EIP-55 address behind a physical confirm before any NS write; show>1 rejected; account_index bounded to 0..=255
has.notes: show=0 (default) lets an unlocked host enumerate all 256 account addresses with no on-device round-trip — a documented privacy trade-off, not a fund risk.

has.item: F-17 signing rate limiter (≥1 s between signs, 250 signs per unlock session, SRAM-only, reset on unlock) gates every C10 sign so a USB-driven burst cannot harvest SCA traces quickly
has.notes: Power-cycle + re-PIN resets the session cap; a flash-persistent daily quota was deferred (sign_rate.rs:36-39).

has.item: Fuzzing/proof coverage of the host-reachable parsers: libFuzzer targets `hid_frame_assembler`, `apdu_parse_header` (+11 others), always-on proptest `fuzz_props` in shared, 4 Kani harnesses over process_frame/ChainState/parse_apdu_header with NO kani::assume on assembler state, mutation-gated; ClusterFuzzLite PR (300 s) + batch (1800 s) ASan; CI runs the fuzz workspace's deterministic suites
has.notes: Coverage stops at the shared crate: the NS router (commands.rs, 1274 LOC) is host-uncompilable and unfuzzed (#313a, #588). docs/STATUS.md:103 records CI as red for long stretches, so CI-executed fuzz evidence is partially suspended.

has.item: GTZC enforcement validation driver: NS probes every NS-alias of a TZSC-secured peripheral (11 on pq1 incl. I2C4/TIM2/TIM3/UCPD1) and asserts delta == PROBES.len() via the e2e-only `nsc_tzic_status` veneer; `make gtzc-enforcement-hw`
evidence: nonsecure/src/main.rs:38-49 (board must be named for gtzc-test)
has.notes: Runs on `mock-se,ui-semihosting,debug-log,e2e-test` — not the shipping combo; SPI1 (SECCFGR2) and IWDG bits are untested by it (#390). TZIC_STATUS veneer compiled out of production.

has.item: Gateway-ABI join check (`tools/check-gateway-abi.sh`) that detects an NS image linked against a previous secure build's veneer addresses (the 2026-09-18 +0x700 incident)
has.notes: Not referenced from the Makefile or any workflow (grep empty); relink-guard gaps in `all/nonsecure` and `bootproof-build` recipes tracked in #690.

has.item: Non-production gateway surface fenced out: prodtest INS/veneers behind `prodtest` (incompatible with mode-production, bhk, tamp-wipe, tzic-wipe, real OTP roots); CMD_TEST_PIN_LOCKOUT and CMD_TZIC_STATUS behind `e2e-test` (mutually exclusive with mode-production); `make prod-feature-check` denylist
has.notes: #735: the denylist covers only 1 of 3 firmware crates and misses the #705 OVP experiment features.

has.item: CMD_GET_PIN_ATTEMPT_LOG (INS 0x03): read-only RAM-resident reason ring, deliberately readable WITHOUT PIN on a locked device so a shipped unit's lockout can be explained (#715)
has.notes: Owner decision on shipping it unauthenticated is OPEN (#719). Uses a bare `if !validate_ns_write_ptr` and no HandlerGuard — the only production handler not sentinel-gated. Missing from the INS table in usb-protocol-v2.md.

has.item: Intrusion-wipe path does a USB soft-disconnect before reset so the host sees a clean detach/re-attach; GET_STATUS no longer carries the constant-1 `provisioned` byte (X17-UC2)

On-silicon USB transport e2e: `fwup-transport-hw` (BEGIN+CHUNK+COMMIT round-trip over real HID), `fwup-transport-hw-iwdg` (idle survival with IWDG live), host scripts hid_sign*.py / hid_smoke.py / fwup-transport-test.py; USB signing proven on pq1 silicon
has.notes: These are happy-path/robustness receipts, not adversarial USB testing (see gap: #590).

has.item: NS-side trailer-skeleton normalisation: NS pads missing u16 trailer prefixes with [0,0] so a short companion payload degrades to unknown-token/blind-sign rather than misaligning the secure parser; NS never looks up metadata (DBs are host-side, device holds only Merkle roots)
has.notes: NS mutates the payload it forwards (writes zero prefixes into CHAIN_BUF) — benign because the secure parser re-validates every trailer against pinned roots, but it is an NS-authored byte range crossing the gateway.

gaps.gap: Absolute chain/drain lifetime bounds and the RX reassembly timeout are driven by the host-controlled OTG_DSTS.FNSOF clock, which freezes during USB suspend; the F11 lease and partial state survive arbitrary wall time while suspended. IWDG cannot help (the NS loop keeps running).
gaps.notes: Design note, not a keepalive vector (host cannot send frames while suspended).

gaps.tracked_in: #390 (C3), #79 (IWDG silicon), #80 (RCC/PWR), #53 (GPDMA/GPIO), #269 (tz-3), #95 (bind SAU config to validator constants)

gaps.gap: No privilege separation inside either world: NS runs as privileged thread (CONTROL_NS=0, boot_ns.rs:36-40) with no MPU; no NS MPU or secure MPU configuration exists anywhere (grep MPU in secure/src, nonsecure/src empty); attacker-data parsers (ERC-7730 walker, typed-call ABI, EIP-712 decoders) run fully privileged in the secure world.

gaps.gap: FI-hardening uniformity at the gateway: `NsPtr<T>` typestate adopted by one veneer only; `cmd_pin_attempt_log.rs:23` is a production, PIN-less handler with a bare `if !validate_ns_write_ptr` (no sentinel, no HandlerGuard) — the exact FAIL-OUT shape the 2026-06-11 HIGH-1 pass removed elsewhere; prodtest.rs now has 15 bare gates (issue says 12).

gaps.gap: IWDG liveness gaps: boot-grace kicks forever until NS registers a heartbeat; heartbeat registration veneer is re-callable from NS; no watchdog before post-unlock init; and a USB flood (live loop) is not a stall so IWDG never fires — the HID OUT token bucket that would have bounded floods was descoped.
gaps.tracked_in: #176 (F31/RUN-3); flood case documented as accepted in threat-model.md:374
gaps.notes: Re-open a rate bucket only with profiling evidence that RX-FIFO NAK backpressure does not absorb the flood (owner rationale 2026-05-28).

gaps.gap: Two security gates exist as scripts but are not executed by CI/Makefile: `make check-fi-ir` (IR gate for fi_min, issue #130) is absent from every workflow; `tools/check-gateway-abi.sh` (stale-veneer ABI join) has no Makefile/CI caller; two hardware recipes still miss the relink guard.
gaps.tracked_in: #690 (relink guard), #130 (still OPEN though fix landed), #701 (ABI gate promotion)
gaps.notes: A stale-veneer NS image booted and enumerated normally on 2026-09-18 and then faulted the secure world on the first APDU.

gaps.gap: Prompt-fatigue DoS on a LOCKED device: INS 0x10 UNLOCK pops the trusted PIN dialog every time and nothing rate-limits a host that keeps issuing it (F3 idempotency only covers the UNLOCKED state); each pop also arms a fresh 120 s input window (cmd_request_unlock.rs:46). No attempt is burned unless the user types, so this is UX/DoS, but it trains the user to see unsolicited PIN prompts.
gaps.tracked_in: UNTRACKED — nearest is #600 (signing-ceremony anomaly layer, sign path only)
gaps.notes: Also: the PendSV re-unlock loop blocks NS/USB for up to 120 s per pass while the PIN prompt is up (#700/#692).

gaps.gap: PendSV idle re-unlock loop: runaway guard (12 passes / 3 verdictless) never exercised on silicon; on e2e images a persistent SE fault still burns the 10-attempt budget; NS/USB starved while the loop blocks in enter_pin.
gaps.notes: Root cause of the 2026-09-21 'PIN locked after a correct PIN' incident is still unidentified.

gaps.gap: After 120 s idle the SysTick ISR performs a full FI-hardened TRNG draw every 1 ms to evaluate `timeout::is_idle() && nsc::is_unlocked()` (always false when locked), degrading UI render cost by +55% and consuming entropy — a self-inflicted resource drain reachable by simply leaving the device plugged in.

No host↔device transport authentication or encryption (no Noise/THP pairing): any process with WebHID/hidapi access to the device is a full peer; the device is origin-blind. Accepted by design because PIN/seed/keys never cross USB and every signable artifact is clear-signed on-device.
gaps.tracked_in: No issue found (gh search for Noise/THP/pairing/'transport encryption' returns only unrelated SE issues); rationale lives in docs/architecture/trezor-comparison.md:722-732 and memory note 'Noise_XX encryption deferred'
gaps.notes: Residual is observability of user behaviour + unsolicited prompts, not fund extraction.

gaps.gap: Device identity over USB is placeholder: FW_VERSION is a fixed 3.0.0 (commands.rs:178-182), device_uid is 16 zero bytes (commands.rs:420-421), USB serial is the constant '0001' (usb/mod.rs:200); there is no USB-reachable device attestation so a companion cannot distinguish a genuine unit from a clone over the wire.
gaps.tracked_in: #249/#22 (supply-chain + provisioning attestation, triple-UID binding), partially #353 (wire-v2 bump)
gaps.notes: usb-protocol-v2.md:280-282 honestly warns companions not to key on fw_version; companion-app-integration.md:243 says 'STM32 UID96; zeros on dev builds' though production code also writes zeros.

gaps.gap: Firmware-root ↔ companion-catalogue pairing (ERC-7730/ERC-20 descriptor sets the companion supplies) is unauthenticated on the wire; a companion with the wrong catalogue degrades to blind-sign/refusal rather than a wrong render, but the pairing itself is not asserted.
gaps.notes: Device verifies every bundle against pinned Merkle roots, so this is a UX/availability gap, not a WYSIWYS break.

gaps.gap: Error-mimicry / repeat-ceremony attack: a hostile companion can manufacture repeated 'failed, sign again' occasions and mutate the payload between retries; no on-device repeat-prompt detector or retry-mutation flag exists.

Memory note project_usb_hid.md states 'GTZC TZSC marks USB OTG FS + GPIOA + GPIOB + UCPD1 as non-secure'. Code: UCPD1 is SECURE on both boards (sau.rs:289-314), GPIO attribution is per-pin via GPIOx_SECCFGR not TZSC (usb_hw.rs:156-174), and only PA11/PA12 are NS on pq1.
owner_decisions: USB OTG FS stays in the NS world and NS-attributed in GTZC (sau.rs:375-383); the device deliberately uses OTG_FS (no DMA) and migration to OTG_HS is an architectural ban requiring a redone threat analysis (threat-model.md:379, production-security.md:332-335). Do not propose moving USB into the secure world or onto HS.

HID OUT token-bucket rate limiter DESCOPED-WITH-RATIONALE 2026-05-28: a ~200 reports/s cap false-trips legitimate chained transfers (8 KB FW_BEGIN ≈ 33 frames in ~165 ms). Re-open only if profiling shows a USB-level DoS that DWC2 RX-FIFO NAK backpressure does not absorb (threat-model.md:374).

NS does not control the inactivity timer (CLAUDE.md 'What NOT to do'; timeout.rs:18-21). The single sanctioned carve-out is #713: REQUEST_UNLOCK arms the input window only when the device is LOCKED with no secret loaded (cmd_request_unlock.rs:33-49).

Firmware is stateless w.r.t. slot selection (invariant #8): `(chain_id, slot_index, flags, account_index)` are companion-supplied on every sign by design; defense is derivation binding + sender binding, not refusing companion input. Do not propose on-device slot state.

GET_STATUS `provisioned` byte was deleted (X17-UC2) rather than adding a provisioning-state veneer (rejected as too heavy and too much new NS-callable surface); companions detect the blank state from the on-device wizard (commands.rs:436-453, usb-protocol-v2.md:264-269).

CMD_GET_PIN_ATTEMPT_LOG ships in production and is readable WITHOUT the PIN on a locked device, deliberately; the exposure is an owner decision tracked in #719 — 'do not gate or ungate it here without that decision' (pin_attempt_log.rs:32-37).

EIP-1271 RAW32 stays an intentionally opaque, loudly-labelled blind tier; companions MUST NOT downgrade typed data to RAW32; disabling RAW32 in production is the preferred policy unless an explicit compatibility decision accepts the residual (CLAUDE.md; #381 ship-blocker decision open).

A Trezor `secmon`-style secure/NS split is declined on principle (secmon trusts NS for what-you-sign = the blind-digest oracle PQSigner forbids); only an intra-secure MPU-lite privilege split of attacker-data parsers is a candidate, ranked DESIGN L–XL, low priority (#277; trezor-comparison critical-port C-1).

Host↔device transport encryption/authentication (Noise/THP pairing) is deferred by design: PIN, seed, and keys never cross USB; the device is origin-blind and relies entirely on on-device clear-signing + physical confirm (trezor-comparison.md:722-732; usb-companion playbook §A2 posture).

Debug instrumentation may ship in this bring-up branch (CLAUDE.md pre-production caveat): NS pre-USB register dumps are DHCSR-gated (nonsecure/src/main.rs:180-208); CI must gate production on debug-log/e2e-test/mock-se/otp-hardcoded-master-key/ui-capture OFF; `make prod-check` is expected to stop at the rollback quarantine (Makefile:2769-2777).

Shipping dual-SE images force `tamp` + `tamp-wipe` + `tzic-wipe` (MEDIUM-1 fence) so a single NS→S illegal access is a tamper-class event that wipes; HardFault/unexpected-IRQ deliberately do NOT arm the destructive SE wipe (a glitch must not become an unrecoverable brick) — main.rs HardFault doc comment.

ML-KEM-1024 inner wrap for the SE tunnels was DESCOPED 2026-07-07 (owner decision, do not re-raise — CLAUDE.md invariant #3); not a USB item but constrains any 'add PQ KEM to the host transport' proposal: the accepted model is symmetric-rooted tunnels and no Shor material on any bus.
TROPIC01 removed 2026-07-14 (dual-SE only); SPI2 'stays NS on the non-LCD Tropic bench build' comments in sau.rs are historical — do not resurrect a third SE bus into the GTZC allowlist.
